about: With every setting at its default, an archive of a change that has a pull request now prints one more line when it commits a file from the change's folder that git never tracked, naming that file. The archive's own requirement always said it would; it never did until the change seam-chaining-grants. G0 says a default install behaves exactly as before, except for behaviours the user names.
question: Should G0 name the archive's line about untracked files as a second ratified exception, or record it as the repair of a promise the archive's requirement already made, outside what G0 governs?
detail: src/core/pr/tail.ts observations.carried_untracked and the pr-archive-tail reference's naming line, landed in 2026-11-11-seam-chaining-grants on the user's answer to stop-2026-11-11T02-01-18Z (that change's trail). R-adf-11 names the first exception (the decision-reading reader).
